source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use an individualized furosemide dose and monitor clinical response, kidney function, volume status, and electrolytes.","B":"Assume thiazides are always ineffective in chronic kidney disease, regardless of kidney function or treatment goal.","C":"Select the loop diuretic because it requires no dose adjustment or monitoring when kidney function is impaired.","D":"Use a fixed high-dose regimen for every client with kidney disease, because response is independent of clinical status."}}
source_row.rationale: Furosemide dosing and monitoring are individualized; kidney function, volume status, electrolyte balance and clinical diuretic response matter. A categorical claim that one diuretic class is always effective or ineffective at a given renal level is inappropriate.
source_row.source_detail: Dosage/administration and warnings sections: therapy is individualized; monitor fluid/electrolyte balance and renal function, with dosage titrated to response and clinical need. DailyMed FDA labeling, updated June 17, 2026; rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: A client with edema and chronic kidney disease is prescribed furosemide. Which nursing principle is most accurate?
